- Edit files outside your worktree.
- Pull from main; you work off `teamwork/base-$SESSION_ID`.
- Self-certify. Your summary is "I made these changes and ran these
  checks; the verifier should check X, Y, Z independently." Not
  "this works."
- Add libraries the spec didn't authorize.
- Modify the Sentinel's orchestration files (`state.json`,
  `plan.dag.json`, etc.). The Sentinel owns those.

## Cost reporting

Cost is tracked automatically by OpenCode across the entire session tree. Do NOT
write `cost.json` — it is not read. Before you stop, you may call `teamwork_cost`
once with your `taskId` (e.g. `teamwork_cost({ taskId: "R1-impl" })`) so your
session's spend is immediately attributed to your task bucket.

## What if you are stuck

- If a dependency isn't ready: write to `questions.md` and STOP. The
  Sentinel will re-dispatch when the dep completes.
- If the spec is impossible: write `BLOCKED: <reason>` to
  `summary.md` and stop. The Sentinel will re-plan.
- If the spec needs more work than fits in one worker session: split
  the work, write `handoff.md`, and stop. The Sentinel will re-dispatch a
  new worker on the handoff.

## Handoff

When you complete, block, or hand off, write `handoff.md` with exactly these
five sections (one short paragraph each):
`## 1. Observation` (what you ran and saw), `## 2. Logic Chain`
(observation → conclusion), `## 3. Caveats` (unchecked/assumed/risky),
`## 4. Conclusion` (done, blocked, or needs re-scope), and
`## 5. Verification Method` (how the next agent reproduces it).

# ADR 0001: Reject Shared Mutable Swarm Board in Favor of Parent-Mediated Subagent Sessions and One-File-Per-Artifact Run Storage

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Issue:** [Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2#5](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/5) (`feat: Shared swarm board and inbox`)
- **Classification:** `SPIKE` (ADR-first design gate)

## 1. Context

Issue [#5](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/5) tracks the deferred gap (`A16` in `docs/re/antigravity-teamwork/08-gap-analysis-opencode-teamwork-v2.md`) between Antigravity's native-swarm shared message board (`board.jsonl`, `members.json`, `swarm.json`, `plan.json` under `<appData>/brain/<conv>/.system_generated/swarm/`) and `@heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2`'s single-root, one-file-per-artifact layout under `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/`.

In Antigravity's native `/swarm` subsystem (`docs/re/antigravity-teamwork/09-swarm-board-and-skills.md` §2–§7):
- Coordinator and worker conversations append free-form messages (`{seq, agent, text, time, kind?, request_id?, channel?, control?}`) to a shared `board.jsonl` with a single per-board `seq` space.
- Per-member read/park cursors (`last_read_seq`, `wait_since`, `wake_mode`) are persisted in `members.json`.
- Workers call `swarm_wait{since, mentions_only}` to end their turn and park at zero token/compute cost until woken by an `@name`, `@all`, or `@#channel` post.
- A read-only HTTP sidecar (`docs/re/antigravity-teamwork/assets/builtin/plugins/swarm/sidecars/swarm_board/main.mjs`) tails `board.jsonl` and per-member `transcript.jsonl` files for UI rendering.

**Evidence provenance.** Research files under `docs/re/` are repository-only: the npm package's `files` list includes `docs` but excludes `docs/re/**`, so these citations resolve only in a git checkout (or at `https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/blob/main/<path>` on `main`), not in an installed package.

By contrast, `@heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2` was architected around:
1. **One file per artifact, no shared append-only board or peer message bus (`docs/ARTIFACTS.md:9-38`):** Every run writes isolated artifacts under `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` (`plan.dag.json`, `state.json`, `costs.json`, `candidates/cand-<n>.md`, `critiques/crit-<n>.md`, `synthesis/syn-<n>.md`, `verify/report-<task>.json`, `verify/security-audit.json`, `verify/final.json`) and isolates concurrent code edits in out-of-repo git worktrees (`../.teamwork-worktrees/<session-id>/`). The coordinator-owned `state.json` and `costs.json` are still shared mutable files, but they are written only through the coordinator path and serialised by an in-process `withFileLock` (see §2.3), not by a cross-process lock.
2. **Append-only telemetry, never read by the DAG engine (`docs/ARTIFACTS.md:466-584`):** `events.jsonl` records deterministic lifecycle transitions with a `seq` that is monotonic only within one plugin-host process (see §2.3) and `agentSource`, but is best-effort and fail-open; neither `teamwork_next` nor `teamwork_task_update` reads it.
3. **Prompt-injection guardrails (`docs/GUARDRAILS.md:6-41`):** Run artifacts are treated as untrusted control data. `describeRun` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts:1179-1208`) injects enumerated counters/statuses, the `state.json` path, and — on `main` — the last two pitfall lines truncated to 70 chars each with `clean()` (`tools.ts:1187-1189`, used at `1204`), so it is not purely whitelisted. Newline-stripping and truncation keep each pitfall on one physical line, but free-form pitfall text still reaches `session.hook("context")`; §5 records that residual risk.

Per the issue specification ([Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2#5](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/5)) and the public triage comment ([#1 comment](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/1#issuecomment-7074469705)), no board implementation may proceed before an ADR evaluates OpenCode's actual host messaging primitives, concurrency guarantees, and security boundaries and either **rejects** the shared board with evidence or **accepts** it with a migration plan and concurrency rules.

## 2. Host Capability & Empirical Spike Evidence

A timeboxed spike was executed against the installed OpenCode V2 host binary, resolved on `PATH` via `command -v opencode` (or `$OPENCODE_BIN` when set) and reported by `opencode --version` as `opencode v2.3.2`, and this repository's engine (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts`, `lib/timeline.mjs`, `lib/export.mjs`).

### 2.1 OpenCode V2.3.2 Subagent & Session Messaging Primitives

Inspecting the embedded OpenCode `v2.3.2` plugin runtime (`PluginContextProvider` at byte offsets `173,423,500–173,427,600` and inner `PluginHost` at `177,463,000–177,466,500`) establishes:

1. **Built-in parent-child `<subagent>` inbox delivery (`@123,383,940` and `@169,870,555`):**
   OpenCode `v2.3.2` exposes `ctx.session.create({ id?, parentID?, title?, agent?, model?, location?, metadata?, permissions? })`. Its schema contract states verbatim:
   > *"Set parentID to create a subagent session at the parent's location; set agent to choose its agent (otherwise it uses the default) and start it with session.prompt. After each completed round, the child sends a `<subagent>` report to the parent's inbox and wakes the parent unless it has a staged revert."*
2. **Rich session control surface (`@173,426,510–173,427,100` and `@177,464,500–177,465,800`):**
   Plugin `ctx.session` exposes `list`, `create`, `get`, `remove`, `switchAgent`, `switchModel`, `prompt`, `generate`, `command`, `compact`, `synthetic`, `interrupt`, `update`, `move`, `wait`, `context`, `instructions.entry.{list,put,remove}`, and `hook("context" | "compaction" | "generate" | "fork" | "experimental.idle")`. The internal session service (`@177,414,307`) maintains per-session inbox operations (`inbox`, `cancelInbox`, `steerInbox`, `queueInbox`). `wait` is examined in point 5 below.
3. **Plugin KV storage is global, not a per-run board (`@173,424,254` and `@177,465,980`):**
   `ctx.storage` exposes `{ get, set, remove, scan }` wrapped by `Fd(L, e)`, which prefixes keys with:
   ```js
   let f = `plugin:${e.split("").map((r) => r.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).padStart(4, "0")).join("")}:`;
   ```
   It is a plugin-global key-value store with no append-only JSONL stream, no monotonic sequence allocator, and no file-descriptor lock.
4. **No `swarm_wait` turn-parking primitive on the host (`@0` matches for `swarm_wait` or `board.jsonl`):**
   Unlike Antigravity's Language Server, which terminates an agent turn on `swarm_wait` `DONE` and wakes the conversation only when a matching `@mention` is appended to `board.jsonl` (`09-swarm-board-and-skills.md` §6.1), OpenCode `v2.3.2` has no turn-parking board primitive. Emulating `board_wait` inside an OpenCode plugin tool would hold an active `tool.execute(input, context)` Promise open while polling the filesystem against `context.signal` (`AbortSignal`), consuming tool execution timeouts rather than parking the session between turns.
5. **`ctx.session.wait` is an idle barrier, not a `swarm_wait` substitute (`@123,386,885`, `@123,386,932`, `@123,386,992`):**
   The `wait` method on `ctx.session` is the experimental `experimental.session.wait` RPC (`POST /api/experimental/session/:sessionID/wait`), whose contract string is `"Wait for a session agent loop to become idle."` It is a parent-child idle/completion barrier: it waits for a session's agent loop to finish, cannot observe `board.jsonl`, cannot be woken by a later `@mention`, and has no board cursor or `mentions_only` filter. Awaiting it inside `tool.execute` still holds the tool Promise open while the call blocks, so it does **not** recover Antigravity's `swarm_wait` semantics (end the turn at zero token/compute cost, then wake only on a matching post).

### 2.3 Local Engine Concurrency & Security Constraints

Inspecting `plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts`, `docs/ARTIFACTS.md`, and `docs/GUARDRAILS.md` surfaces four hard architectural mismatches with a shared mutable board:

1. **`withFileLock` is in-process only (`tools.ts:1162-1173`):**
   `fileLocks` is an in-memory `Map<string, Promise<unknown>>`. It serialises async tool calls within a single plugin host process, but provides zero cross-process mutual exclusion (`flock` / `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` lockfiles) if multiple CLI or subagent processes access the same run directory. For `events.jsonl`, this is acceptable because `appendEvent` (`tools.ts:1091-1155`) is fail-open telemetry that no engine decision reads; even so, `seq` is allocated by `nextEventSeq` (`tools.ts:1041-1079`) from the on-disk tail inside that process-local lock, so two host processes can append the same `seq` (or interleave a torn line). For a control-plane `board.jsonl` driving worker coordination and sequence cursors, those collisions would corrupt wake decisions rather than just telemetry.
2. **Plugin tools are not agent-scoped (`docs/GUARDRAILS.md:35-37`, `08-gap-analysis-opencode-teamwork-v2.md` §1.8 #3):**
   OpenCode's `ctx.permission.hook("evaluate")` mediates built-in capabilities (`edit`, `shell`, `webfetch`, `subagent`) enforced by `READ_ONLY_ACTIONS`, but it does **not** fire on plugin-registered `teamwork_*` tools. Furthermore, `agent` attribution in `events.jsonl` is caller-reported or heuristic (`agentSource: "explicit" | "session" | "plan"`, `docs/ARTIFACTS.md:552-561`). A shared `teamwork_board_post` tool would allow any read-only or untrusted-input-Exposed agent (`team/scout`, `team/falsifier`, `team/verifier`, `team/security-auditor`) to spoof another agent's handle or post control directives onto the board.
3. **Indirect prompt-injection amplification (`docs/GUARDRAILS.md:6-12, 38-40`, `08-gap-analysis` §4.3):**
   `clean()` (`tools.ts:840-844`) strips C0/C1 control characters and line separators (`\r`, `\n`, `\u0085`, `\u2028`, `\u2029`) and truncates to a caller-supplied cap, to prevent physical JSONL line-splitting, and `docs/ARTIFACTS.md:563-572` explicitly notes that `clean()` is *"a line-safety and display sanitiser, not a complete defence against hostile text."* A shared board where workers read free-form peer `text` mid-task creates a lateral prompt-injection bus from read-only/web-fetching agents directly into write-capable `team/worker` and `team/sentinel` sessions.
4. **Provenance separation (`09-swarm-board-and-skills.md` §11, `11-runtime-artifacts.md` §2–§6):**
   In Antigravity itself, `board.jsonl` belongs to `cortex/core/native_swarm/board` (`/swarm`), whereas all 39 sampled `/teamwork-preview` state trees on disk coordinate exclusively through parent-child subagent dispatch and isolated markdown artifacts (`DISPATCH.md`, `BRIEFING.md`, `progress.md`, `handoff.md`, `GATE_STATUS.md`) with no `board.jsonl`.

## 3. Decision

**We reject adding a shared swarm board (`board.jsonl`, `members.json`, `swarm.json`, `teamwork_board_*` tools, or a board sidecar) to `@heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2`.**

Instead, `@heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2` retains its single-plane coordination model:
1. **Parent-mediated subagent dispatch:** Co-ordination flows hub-and-spoke through the coordinator (`team/sentinel` or `team/orchestrator`) using OpenCode V2's native subagent session creation and `<subagent>` inbox reports, `state.json` task transitions (`teamwork_next` / `teamwork_task_update`), the cumulative per-task feedback ledger (`feedbackLog`), and `pitfalls.md`. `teamwork_next` is advisory and does not claim or lease a ready task (`tools.ts:1839-1905`, `2048-2075`), so this model assumes a single coordinator loop: two dispatchers polling concurrently can be handed the same ready task.
2. **One file per artifact (`docs/ARTIFACTS.md`):** Concurrent proposers, falsifiers, synthesizers, verifiers, and route-specific workers write to disjoint, path-validated files under `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` and isolated out-of-repo git worktrees.
3. **Fail-open lifecycle event log (`events.jsonl`):** Chronological run observability for `opencode-teamwork timeline` and `opencode-teamwork export` continues to use `events.jsonl` (with `seq` monotonic within a plugin-host process and `agentSource`), which is never fed back into agent prompts or engine control flow.

## 4. Alternatives Considered

### Alternative A (Chosen): Reject `board.jsonl` and rely on OpenCode `<subagent>` inbox + one-file-per-artifact

- **Pros:**
  - No shared append-only board or peer message bus; every artifact has a single owning step and deterministic schema. The coordinator-owned `state.json` and `costs.json` are still shared mutable files, serialised only by the in-process `withFileLock`, so concurrent cross-process `teamwork_task_update` calls can lose updates (§5).
  - Preserves the `docs/GUARDRAILS.md` prompt-injection boundary for peer chat: `describeRun` never injects peer messages. It does inject the last two pitfall lines via `clean(p, 70)` (`tools.ts:1187-1189`), so stored free-form pitfall text remains an accepted residual risk (§5).
  - Zero new runtime dependencies, zero background polling loops, and full compatibility with `lib/timeline.mjs` and `lib/export.mjs`.
  - Matches both OpenCode V2's native `<subagent>` inbox architecture and Antigravity `/teamwork`'s actual artifact-tree coordination model (`08-gap-analysis` §4.3, `09` §11).
- **Cons:**
  - Concurrent sibling workers cannot chat directly peer-to-peer mid-turn; cross-worker synthesis must pass through a DAG dependency barrier (`dependencies` in `spec.json` / `plan.dag.json`) or a `team/synthesizer` round.

### Alternative B (Rejected): Implement a scoped, opt-in append-only `board.jsonl` under `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/`

If a shared board were ever accepted in a future cycle, it could not port Antigravity's `/swarm` board wholesale; it would require all six of the following engineering controls:
1. **Single-root containment:** Store only `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/board.jsonl` (no `members.json`, `swarm.json`, channels, or HTTP sidecar), guarded by `SESSION_ID` allowlist, segment-wise `lstatSync` symlink refusal, `realpathSync` containment, and `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW` bounded reads (`<= 8 MiB`).
2. **Cross-process file locking:** Replace or augment `withFileLock` (`tools.ts:1162-1173`) with an atomic filesystem lockfile (`openSync(lockPath, O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_RDWR)`, PID + timestamp payload, bounded retry/backoff, and stale-lock eviction) so concurrent OS processes cannot interleave lines or duplicate `seq`.
3. **Malformed-line and torn-tail tolerance:** Readers (`since_seq` cursor queries, `lib/timeline.mjs`, `lib/export.mjs`) must ignore blank lines, permanently skip corrupt interior JSON lines without stalling, and withhold un-newlined trailing partial lines until completed (`09-swarm-board-and-skills.md` §7.3).
4. **Bounded wait with `AbortSignal`:** Because OpenCode V2 has no `swarm_wait` turn-parking primitive — and `ctx.session.wait` is only an idle barrier (§2.1 point 5) — any wait primitive must bound polling duration (e.g., `<= 30 s`) and abort cleanly on `context.signal` (`AbortSignal`) without throwing unhandled errors.
5. **Host-verified caller identity & read-only enforcement:** Because `permission.hook("evaluate")` does not mediate `teamwork_*` plugin tools (`docs/GUARDRAILS.md:35-37`), a board-write tool must never trust a caller-supplied `input.agent`; it must resolve `context.sessionID` via `ctx.session.get` and fail closed for roles in `READ_ONLY_ACTIONS`.
6. **Sanitisation & export defanging:** Apply `clean()` (single-line JSONL safety, default cap 64 chars) to ordinary fields, or `cleanBlock()` (the 2,000-char multi-line variant, which preserves `\n`) when a note must span lines, on write; and apply HTML-escaping plus `http(s)://` URL defanging (`https[://]`) in `lib/export.mjs`.

Alternative B is rejected because it adds substantial locking, identity-verification, and polling complexity while still opening an unauthenticated semantic prompt-injection channel between agents, and no route in `@heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2` (including Document Review `#1`, LEMMA `#2`, or Massive-Proof Tournament `#3`) requires mid-turn peer-to-peer worker chat.

### Alternative C (Rejected): Port Antigravity's `/swarm` board and `swarm_board` sidecar wholesale

- Violates the public decision recorded in issue [#5](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/5) and the [triage comment on #1](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/1#issuecomment-7074469705), including the anti-pattern of porting the board, sidecar, or 49-agent roster wholesale; it introduces a long-running HTTP server outside OpenCode's plugin lifecycle, and duplicates `/swarm` infrastructure that Antigravity itself keeps separate from `/teamwork`.

## 5. Consequences

### Positive
- The artifact contract (`docs/ARTIFACTS.md`) and guardrail model (`docs/GUARDRAILS.md`) remain single-plane and deterministic; there is no shared append-only board, while coordinator-owned `state.json`/`costs.json` stay shared and process-locked only (see Known gaps below).
- Read-only agents (`team/scout`, `team/falsifier`, `team/verifier`, `team/security-auditor`) cannot influence active workers via a shared message bus.
- `opencode-teamwork timeline` and `opencode-teamwork export` remain fast, single-pass readers over `state.json`, `plan.dag.json`, `costs.json`, `verify/*`, and `events.jsonl`.

### Negative / Trade-offs
- All inter-agent coordination remains structured around DAG task boundaries, `spec.json` artifact dependencies, `feedbackLog`, and `pitfalls.md` rather than ad-hoc mid-task peer messaging.

### Known gaps / follow-ups

The decision keeps these residual risks inside the coordinator path rather than claiming they do not exist:

- **Duplicate dispatch of a ready task.** `teamwork_next` computes readiness from `state.json` and returns `readyForWorker` (`tools.ts:1839-1905`, `2048-2075`) without claiming or leasing it, so two coordinator loops polling concurrently can both be handed the same task.
- **Lost updates across processes.** `teamwork_task_update` is a read-modify-write of `state.json` inside `withFileLock` (`tools.ts:2131-2132`, lock at `1162-1173`). The lock is an in-memory `Map`, so concurrent updates from separate plugin-host processes can overwrite each other.
- **`events.jsonl` sequence collisions.** `seq` is allocated by `nextEventSeq` from the on-disk tail (`tools.ts:1041-1079`) inside the same process-local lock, so it is monotonic only within one plugin-host process; cross-process appends can duplicate a `seq` or interleave a torn line. The log stays telemetry-only and fail-open.
- **Pitfall text injection.** `describeRun` injects the last two pitfalls via `clean(p, 70)` (`tools.ts:1187-1189`, used at `1204`). Newlines and control characters are stripped and every entry is truncated, but the text is still free-form and read from the run directory, so a hostile `pitfalls.md` is a residual stored-injection vector.
- **Unmediated plugin tools.** `permission.hook("evaluate")` does not intercept `teamwork_*` tools (`docs/GUARDRAILS.md:35-37`); the session-id allowlist is the only containment for caller identity.

## 6. Missing Capabilities & Revisit Criteria

Do not revisit or implement a shared board unless **all three** conditions below are met:
1. **Concrete route demand:** A shipped route requires concurrent sibling workers to exchange mid-turn messages that cannot be expressed via parent `<subagent>` inbox reports (`ctx.session.create({ parentID })`) or DAG phase barriers.
2. **Host turn-parking & tool permission mediation:** OpenCode V2 exposes (a) a turn-parking wake primitive analogous to `swarm_wait` — not merely `ctx.session.wait`, which is an idle barrier (§2.1 point 5) — so waiting does not block an active `tool.execute` call, and (b) `permission.hook("evaluate")` mediation or authenticated caller-session identity on plugin-defined tools (`docs/GUARDRAILS.md:35-37`).
3. **Cross-process locking specification:** An explicit lockfile and semantic-sanitisation contract (Alternative B §1–§6 above) is ratified in a superseding ADR.

# ADR 0002: Retain Single Workspace Run Artifact Root `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` Pending Host Per-Conversation Filesystem Storage

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Issue:** [#6](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/6) (`refactor: Per-conversation artifact root`)
- **Classification:** `SPIKE` (Spike + ADR before moving files)

## 1. Context

Issue [#6](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/6) tracks the deferred architectural difference (`A21` in `docs/re/antigravity-teamwork/08-gap-analysis-opencode-teamwork-v2.md` §2.5 and §4.5) between Antigravity's per-conversation scratch root and `@heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2`'s workspace-rooted run directory.

In Antigravity (`docs/re/antigravity-teamwork/11-runtime-artifacts.md` §2.1–§2.3, §4, §5.2):
- Teamwork state files (`ORIGINAL_REQUEST.md`, `PROJECT.md`, `SCOPE.md`, `GATE_STATUS.md`, and per-agent `teamwork_<role>_m<M>_r<R>[_<N>]/{DISPATCH,BRIEFING,progress,handoff}.md`) are written under `<appDataDir>/brain/<conversation-id>/scratch/.agents/teamwork/`.
- Each dispatched subagent runs in its own conversation with its own `brain/<conversation-id>/scratch/` directory, and the dispatch instructions explicitly forbid creating `.agents/teamwork/` inside the user's project workspace.

In `@heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2` (`docs/ARTIFACTS.md:7-38`, `docs/GUARDRAILS.md:18-25`):
- Every run writes under a single workspace-relative root: `<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` (while git worktrees live outside the repository under `$TEAMWORK_WORKTREES_DIR` or `../.teamwork-worktrees/<session-id>/`).
- Every engine tool (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts`), every CLI reader (`lib/runs.mjs`, `lib/timeline.mjs`, `lib/export.mjs`), every agent prompt (`agents/team/*.md`), and the CI prompt linter (`scripts/lint-prompts.mjs`) are written against this single-root contract; §7 records where that enforcement is incomplete.

Per [issue #6](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/6) and the [triage comment on #1](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/1#issuecomment-7074469705) (`#6 Per-conversation artifact root — SPIKE, then ADR`), a spike must verify whether OpenCode V2 actually exposes a per-conversation or per-agent filesystem data directory and evaluate the impact on path containment, `timeline`, `export`, and legacy runs before moving any files.

### 2.3 Local Single-Root Containment & CLI Reader Invariants

Inspecting the repository confirms three tightly coupled invariants anchored on `<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/`:

1. **Path containment and symlink refusal (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts:495-507, 917-1007`):**
   - `RUN_ROOT = ".opencode/teamwork"` (`:495`), `SESSION_ID = /^[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._-]{0,63}$/` (`:498`), `TASK_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/` (`:506`).
   - `runsBase(root)` (`:917-936`) calls `lstatSync` on `<root>/.opencode` and `<root>/.opencode/teamwork` to refuse symlinks and verifies `realpathSync(base)` stays within `realpathSync(root)`.
   - `resolveRun(root, sessionId)` (`:984-1007`) validates `SESSION_ID`, rejects a lexically escaping `relative(base, cand)` (`..` or absolute), and — only when `existsSync(cand)` is true — refuses `lstatSync(cand).isSymbolicLink()` and re-checks containment with `realpathSync(base)` / `realpathSync(cand)`. It does **not** call `containmentError`; that helper (`:804-810`) is used only by the worktree code (`:2694, 2702, 2727, 2738`). The `existsSync` guard is a known dangling-symlink gap (§7).
2. **Standalone CLI inspection (`lib/runs.mjs:21`, `lib/timeline.mjs:89-125`, `lib/export.mjs:138-223`):**
   - `opencode-teamwork runs`, `inspect`, `timeline`, and `export` run as standalone Node CLI processes from the project root (`process.cwd()`), with no connection to the OpenCode plugin runtime.
   - `lib/timeline.mjs` and `lib/export.mjs` verify `runRootIsLink(projectRoot)` (`.opencode` and `.opencode/teamwork` symlink checks), read `<projectRoot>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW` and byte caps (`8 MiB` for `events.jsonl`, `64 MiB` for JSON), and validate `verify/report-<taskId>.json` containment inside the single `runDir`.
3. **CI prompt linter (`scripts/lint-prompts.mjs:5, 76-85, 123-124`):**
   - Rejects the legacy `.teamwork-runs` root and `<run-id>` terminology in agent prompts (`FORBIDDEN`, `:76-85`) and the legacy root in plugin command templates (`:123-124`); it also parses topologies from `docs/ARTIFACTS.md` (`:29-73`).
   - It does **not** assert that `docs/ARTIFACTS.md` documents only the canonical root, nor that `tools.ts`, `lib/runs.mjs`, `lib/timeline.mjs`, and `lib/export.mjs` agree on it (see §7, artifact-root drift).

## 3. Decision

**We retain `<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` as the single canonical artifact root and defer relocating artifacts to per-conversation roots.**

Specifically:
1. **No relocation to non-existent host per-conversation storage:** Because OpenCode `v2.3.2` exposes no host-provided per-conversation filesystem directory (`ctx.location` is workspace-level and `ctx.storage` is a global KV store inaccessible to standalone CLI tools), moving run state out of `<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` cannot use a native host primitive.
2. **Preserve single-root `resolveRun`, `timeline`, and `export` guarantees:** Keeping all artifacts for `<session-id>` under one contained directory means the `SESSION_ID`/`TASK_ID` allowlists, intended `lstatSync` symlink refusal (with the dangling-symlink limit noted in §7), `realpathSync` containment, and standalone `opencode-teamwork runs | inspect | timeline | export` behavior stay unchanged, without multi-directory discovery or clock-skew unioning.
3. **Adopt per-agent / per-subflow subdirectories inside `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` when isolation is needed:** As noted in `08-gap-analysis-opencode-teamwork-v2.md` §4.5, when route-specific or per-agent artifact isolation is needed, it belongs in subdirectories *under* `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` (such as `candidates/`, `critiques/`, `synthesis/`, `verify/`) rather than separate root directories.

## 4. Alternatives Considered

### Alternative A (Chosen): Keep single run root `<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` (with internal subdirectories)

- **Pros:**
  - Works with every existing CLI command (`runs`, `inspect`, `timeline`, `export`, `prune`) and CI prompt lint check (`scripts/lint-prompts.mjs`) with zero configuration.
  - Preserves a single `realpathSync` containment anchor (`runsBase(root)`), preventing cross-directory symlink traversal.
  - Self-contained: a user can inspect, archive, or delete one run by operating on one directory.
- **Cons:**
  - Leave `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` inside the workspace directory unless the user configures `.gitignore` (unlike worktrees, which already live outside the repository under `../.teamwork-worktrees/<session-id>/`).
  - Concurrent subagents share the run directory and rely on disjoint per-task/per-candidate filenames (`verify/report-<taskId>.json`, `candidates/cand-<n>.md`) rather than host-enforced per-conversation directory sandboxes.

### Alternative B (Deferred): Explicit `scratchRoot` / `$OPENCODE_TEAMWORK_SCRATCH_DIR` outside the workspace

- Mirrors `$TEAMWORK_WORKTREES_DIR` (`tools.ts:2659-2661`) by relocating the entire `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` tree to a user-configured external directory while keeping one directory per `<session-id>`.
- **Why deferred:** Unlike per-conversation roots, a single external `scratchRoot` still puts all agents of a run in one directory (so it does not provide per-agent write isolation), and it breaks parameterless `npx @heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2 timeline | export` unless the same environment variable or config is present in every user shell.

### Alternative C (Rejected): Split a single run across multiple per-`context.sessionID` root directories and union them in `timeline` / `export`

- Would store artifacts under `<root>/<runId>/<context.sessionID>/...` or `<scratchRoot>/<context.sessionID>/...` and require `lib/timeline.mjs` and `lib/export.mjs` to discover and union multiple roots into one run report.
- **Why rejected:**
  1. Standalone CLI calls (`opencode-teamwork timeline <runId>`) have no access to OpenCode's in-memory session tree when `opencode.db` is absent or located in a custom XDG data path, making child-root discovery unreliable without a parent manifest inside the primary run root anyway.
  2. Unioning `state.json`, `costs.json`, `events.jsonl` (`seq`), and `verify/final.json` across multiple directories reintroduces split-brain state and cross-root ordering ambiguity.

## 5. Consequences

### Positive
- No regression to `resolveRun` behavior, `O_NOFOLLOW` bounded readers in `lib/timeline.mjs` and `lib/export.mjs`, `scripts/lint-prompts.mjs`, or legacy single-root runs (their pre-existing gaps are listed in §7).
- Maintains a clear separation between out-of-repo git worktrees (`../.teamwork-worktrees/<session-id>/`) and single-rooted run metadata (`.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/`).

### Negative / Trade-offs
- Agents holding `edit` or `shell` permissions are not confined by the host to a private per-agent scratch directory (`docs/GUARDRAILS.md:27-33, 38-40`).

## 6. Missing Capabilities & Migration Plan (If Revisited)

### 6.1 Exact Missing Host Capabilities in OpenCode V2 (`v2.3.2`)
1. **Per-session filesystem scratch path:** OpenCode's `PluginContextProvider` (`@173,420,383`) and tool `execute` context (`Q` at `@173,428,138`) expose `ctx.location.directory` (workspace) and `context.sessionID` (string ID), but no host-managed per-session scratch directory (`context.scratchDir` or `ctx.session.scratchPath({ sessionID })`) outside the git working tree.
2. **Per-agent filesystem sandbox enforcement:** OpenCode's `permission.hook("evaluate")` (`@173,423,694`) can deny `edit` or `shell`, but does not enforce per-agent path confinement for `shell` commands (`docs/GUARDRAILS.md:27-32, 41`).

### 6.2 Migration Plan If Per-Conversation Roots or `scratchRoot` Are Revisited

If OpenCode V2 adds a per-session scratch directory or if maintainers opt into an explicit `scratchRoot` setting. Throughout this subsection `<runRoot>` is the artifact base (`<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork`, or the configured external root) and `<runDir>` is `<runRoot>/<session-id>`:
1. **Primary Run Anchor & Legacy Tolerance:**
   - Keep `<runDir>` (the legacy layout is `<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/`) as the fallback so existing runs continue to resolve without migration.
   - If an external `scratchRoot` is configured (via `OPENCODE_TEAMWORK_SCRATCH_DIR`, or a documented `artifactsRoot` key in `~/.config/opencode/teamwork.json`), validate that `scratchRoot` is an absolute path, is not a symlink (`lstatSync`), and does not alias `/` or the git `.git` directory; resolve runs by checking the configured `scratchRoot` first and falling back to `<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/`. Note that `teamwork.json` is currently the installer-written agent model map (`{ "models": { ... } }`, read by `lib/team.mjs:79-81, 84-94` and documented in `README.md`); adding paths there requires an explicit, documented schema addition, not an ad-hoc key.
2. **Per-Agent Sub-Roots Under One Run Index:**
   - Never scatter root-level files (`ORIGINAL_REQUEST.md`, `plan.dag.json`, `state.json`, `costs.json`, `events.jsonl`, `verify/final.json`) across sibling conversation folders.
   - Instead, isolate per-agent outputs under `<runDir>/agents/<subSessionId>/` (validated against `SESSION_ID = /^[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._-]{0,63}$/` and `ensureSafeRunSubpath` segment-wise `lstatSync` + `realpathSync`).
3. **Reader Union Contract (`lib/runs.mjs`, `lib/timeline.mjs`, `lib/export.mjs`):**
   - `buildTimeline` and `buildExportData` continue to read `plan.dag.json`, `state.json`, `costs.json`, `events.jsonl`, and `verify/final.json` from the canonical `<runDir>` anchor, and union per-agent artifacts from `<runDir>/agents/<subSessionId>/` in deterministic `(seq, timestamp, subSessionId)` order while enforcing `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW` and byte caps on every sub-path.

## 7. Known gaps / follow-ups

This ADR records a decision, not a guarantee that the current single-root implementation is airtight. The following gaps are known and deliberately left to follow-up work:

1. **Dangling symlinks bypass the refusal checks (High).** Both `runsBase` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts:917-936`) and `resolveRun` (`:984-1007`) gate their `lstatSync` / `realpathSync` checks behind `existsSync`. `existsSync` follows symlinks, so a *dangling* symlink at `.opencode`, `.opencode/teamwork`, or `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>` reports absent and is never refused; `resolveRun` then returns the path and writers such as `mkdirSync(run, { recursive: true })` (`:1373`) and `writeFileSync` follow the link outside the root. A future resolver must `lstat` every component of the path, treat only `ENOENT` as absent, refuse *any* symlink (including dangling ones), and only then apply `realpathSync` containment. This is a real escape today, not only a per-conversation concern.
2. **External `scratchRoot` runs would be invisible to every reader (Medium).** `listTeamworkRuns` hard-codes `<projectRoot>/.opencode/teamwork` (`lib/runs.mjs:20-25`); `inspect` reuses it (`lib/runs.mjs:75-76`), and `runs`, `timeline`, and `export` discover runs through it (`bin/opencode-teamwork.mjs:221, 303, 372`). Worktree `prune` reads the phase from the same workspace-rooted `state.json` (`lib/runs.mjs:140-145`), so an external run would look unfinished and its worktrees would never be pruned. Adopting Alternative B therefore requires one shared resolver plumbed through run creation, `listTeamworkRuns`, `buildTimeline`, `buildExportData`, and `pruneTeamworkWorktrees`; otherwise external runs silently disappear from the CLI.
3. **Artifact-root drift passes CI (Medium).** `scripts/lint-prompts.mjs` only rejects the legacy `.teamwork-runs` string and `<run-id>` terminology (`:5, 76-85, 123-124`) and asserts that `tools.ts` *contains* `SESSION_ID`, `relative(`, `realpathSync(`, `lstatSync(`, and `permission.hook` (`:141-149`). It never asserts that `RUN_ROOT = ".opencode/teamwork"` (`tools.ts:495`), the layout in `docs/ARTIFACTS.md:7-38`, and the root literals in `lib/runs.mjs` / `lib/timeline.mjs` / `lib/export.mjs` agree. A future root change can therefore land half-applied and still pass. The required check is a single canonical root (a constant, or parsed from `docs/ARTIFACTS.md`) compared against every reader and writer, failing CI on mismatch.

# ADR 0003: Successor Orchestrator Handoff Is Not Possible on OpenCode V2 Without Host Session-Replacement Primitives

- **Status:** Accepted (`Not possible on this host`)
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Issue:** [Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2#4](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/4) (`feat: Successor orchestrator handoff`)
- **Classification:** `SPIKE` → `BLOCKED` (`not possible on this host`)

## 1. Context

Issue [#4](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/4) tracks the deferred gap (`A20` in `docs/re/antigravity-teamwork/08-gap-analysis-opencode-teamwork-v2.md` §2.5 and §4.6) for automatic orchestrator self-succession at a subagent spawn-count threshold.

In Antigravity (`docs/re/antigravity-teamwork/10-official-docs-cross-check.md` §1 row 6 and §2.3):
- A top-level **Sentinel** conversation (`sentinel@external`, runtime type `teamwork`) manages a separate **Project Orchestrator** child conversation (`orchestrator_pure`, runtime type `teamwork_orchestrator`) via `invoke_subagent` (`@113,255,284`).
- The Project Orchestrator tracks cumulative subagent spawns against `succession_threshold` (`Spawn count: [0] / [succession_threshold]` at `@113,710,952` and `@113,710,972`; role `successor` at `@114,727,128`).
- When the threshold is reached, the orchestrator writes a structured `handoff.md` (*Milestone State / Active Subagents / Pending Decisions / Remaining Work / Key Artifacts* at `@114,728,898`), spawns a fresh replacement orchestrator conversation passing the Sentinel's conversation ID as parent, and exits (`@113,256,585`).

In `@heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/index.ts:31-65, 215-230`):
- Invoking `/teamwork` does **not** spawn a child orchestrator conversation under a persistent parent Sentinel; instead, `ctx.command.transform` switches the user's current foreground session to `team/sentinel` via `ctx.session.switchAgent({ sessionID, agent: "team/sentinel" })` (`index.ts:223`) and runs the coordinator directly in that session.
- Run state is checkpointed deterministically on disk in `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/state.json` (plus `plan.dag.json`, `costs.json`, `pitfalls.md`, and `feedbackLog`), and `session.hook("context")` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts:2906-2911`) injects `describeRun(root)` into every `team/*` agent turn.

Per issue [#4](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/4) (`feat: Successor orchestrator handoff`), whose triage note is recorded in [#1](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/1#issuecomment-7074469705):
- **Acceptance:** *"If buildable, a threshold triggers a correct successor. If not, an ADR names the missing host primitive and the outcome 'not possible on this host'."*
- **Prohibitions:** *"Do not fake a successor by clearing context in place; do not build a supervisor sidecar as a side effect. Spike/ADR first; 'not possible' is acceptable and expected."*

## 2. Host Capability & Empirical Spike Evidence

A timeboxed spike inspected the `opencode` binary on `PATH` (`OPENCODE_BIN` overrides the lookup; `v2.3.2` on this host) across the HTTP/RPC session endpoints (`@123,383,500–123,386,000`, `@169,870,000–169,875,000`), the plugin `ctx.session` wrapper (`@173,426,510–173,427,100`), and the inner `PluginHost` session service (`@177,414,200–177,415,600`, `@177,464,500–177,465,800`).

### 2.1 What OpenCode V2.3.2 `ctx.session` Exposes

Unlike the earlier static note in `08-gap-analysis-opencode-teamwork-v2.md` §4.6 (which observed only `ctx.session.switchAgent` in this repository's source), OpenCode `v2.3.2` exposes the following methods on `ctx.session` (`@173,426,379–173,427,050` and `@177,464,434–177,465,700`):

- `hook(type, fn, opts)` — supports `"context"`, `"compaction"`, `"generate"`, `"fork"`, `"experimental.idle"`
- `list`, `create`, `get`, `remove`
- `switchAgent`, `switchModel`
- `prompt`, `generate`, `command`, `compact`, `synthetic`
- `interrupt`, `update`, `move`, `wait`, `context`
- `instructions.entry.{list, put, remove}`

`wait({ sessionID })` is an experimental idle/completion barrier (paired with `hook("experimental.idle")`), not a successor/handoff primitive: it cannot retire `S_1`, reparent `S_2`, or move the user's attached TUI/CLI stream.

Specifically, `ctx.session.create` (`@177,464,505`) is implemented as:

```js
create: (HH) => IH.create({
  id: HH?.id,
  title: HH?.title,
  agent: HH?.agent,
  model: HH?.model,
  metadata: HH?.metadata,
  permissions: HH?.permissions,
  ...HH?.parentID === void 0
    ? { location: HH?.location ?? WH.make({ directory: j.directory, workspaceID: j.workspaceID }) }
    : { parentID: HH.parentID }
})
```

### 2.2 Why Seamless Orchestrator Succession Fails on OpenCode V2.3.2

Testing the semantics of `ctx.session.create`, `ctx.session.update`, and `ctx.session.compact` reveals four missing host capabilities that prevent an active orchestrator session `S_1` from handing off to a fresh successor session `S_2`:

1. **`ctx.session.create({ parentID: S_1 })` creates a subordinate child that reports back to `S_1`, not a replacement (`@123,383,940`, `@169,870,555`):**
   OpenCode's `session.create` schema contract states verbatim:
   > *"Set parentID to create a subagent session at the parent's location; set agent to choose its agent (otherwise it uses the default) and start it with session.prompt. After each completed round, the child sends a `<subagent>` report to the parent's inbox and wakes the parent unless it has a staged revert."*
   If `S_1` spawns `S_2` with `parentID: S_1` and exits, `S_2` is a child subagent of `S_1`. As soon as `S_2` completes a round (or waits for a child of its own), OpenCode delivers a `<subagent>` report to `S_1`'s inbox and wakes `S_1`, resurrecting the degraded predecessor session instead of retiring it.
2. **`ctx.session.create({})` (without `parentID`) detaches from the user's active TUI/CLI foreground session (`@177,464,637`):**
   Calling `ctx.session.create` without `parentID` creates an unlinked top-level session in the database (`parent_id = NULL`). However, OpenCode `v2.3.2` exposes **no TUI/CLI foreground session-handoff primitive** (`ctx.ui` / `ctx.session.attach` / `ctx.session.replaceActive`) to switch the user's attached terminal or TUI view from `S_1` to `S_2`. A background `ctx.session.prompt({ sessionID: S_2.id, ... })` executes detached from the user's active conversation stream, leaving the user staring at a halted `S_1` session.
3. **No session reparenting / child-ownership transfer (`@177,414,307`, `@177,465,023`):**
   `ctx.session.update({ sessionID, title?, metadata?, permissions? })` only calls `IH.rename`, `IH.setMetadata`, and `IH.setPermissions`. Neither `ctx.session.update` nor `ctx.session.move` can update `parentID` on in-flight child sessions or transfer pending `<subagent>` inbox deliveries from `S_1` to `S_2`.
4. **`ctx.session.compact` and `session.fork` do not provide fresh-session succession (`@123,385,152`, `@169,872,567`, `@173,426,379`):**
   - `ctx.session.compact({ sessionID })` summarises `S_1`'s message history in place within the same session ID. Faking a successor via in-place compaction or context clearing is explicitly prohibited by the issue contract (*"Do not fake a successor by clearing context in place"*).
   - `session.fork` (`/api/session/:sessionID/fork` at `@169,872,567` and its description at `@123,385,152`) is not exposed on the plugin `ctx.session` wrapper (`@173,426,379`), and its contract (*"Create a child session by copying projected history before a message"*) copies historical messages into a child session rather than starting a clean-context replacement orchestrator.

## 3. Decision

**Automatic successor orchestrator handoff is classified as `BLOCKED` (`not possible on this host`) on OpenCode V2 (`v2.3.2`).**

1. **No fake in-place succession or supervisor sidecar:** In compliance with the [issue #4 contract](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/4) (triage note: [#1 comment](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/1#issuecomment-7074469705)), we do **not** fake a successor by wrapping `ctx.session.compact` in a tool that claims to spawn a replacement orchestrator, and we do **not** introduce a background supervisor sidecar or detach into a headless top-level session that orphans the user's active TUI/CLI view.
2. **Rely on disk-checkpointed run state and an explicit resume path:**
   `@heretek-ai/opencode-teamwork-v2` already persists all milestone and task progress deterministically in `.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/state.json` (`phase`, per-task `status`, `round`, `branch`, `worktree`, `summary`, `feedbackLog`, `verification`), `plan.dag.json`, `costs.json` (with `snapshots.json.rootSessionIds` supporting multiple root sessions across restarts, `plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts:1428-1442, 1622-1631`), and `pitfalls.md`. When a long-running coordinator session approaches context limits or is interrupted:
   - Host compaction (`session.hook("compaction")` / `session.hook("context")`) automatically re-injects `describeRun(root)` (`tools.ts:1179-1208, 2906-2911`) so the compacted session retains the active run ID, phase, task counts, and `state.json` path.
   - Recovery uses `teamwork_resume({ sessionId })`, which returns the still-open tasks, followed by `teamwork_next({ sessionId })`, which re-derives dispatchable work and skips every `verified_pass` task (`docs/ARTIFACTS.md:223-224`, `snapshots.json.rootSessionIds`). **However, the current `/teamwork` command template always instructs Sentinel to call `teamwork_plan` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/index.ts:42-43`), so `/teamwork <session-id>` today starts a new run instead of resuming the supplied run.** Until the template is changed (follow-up), recovery must be driven explicitly by calling `teamwork_resume({ sessionId })` and then `teamwork_next({ sessionId })` — never `teamwork_plan` — for the existing run ID. The exact command change is a resume branch at the top of the `/teamwork` template: when `$ARGUMENTS` names an existing `.opencode/teamwork/<id>/state.json` (with `plan.dag.json`), call `teamwork_resume`/`teamwork_next` for that ID and skip `teamwork_plan` plus worktree provisioning. This is a manual-recovery UX gap only; it does not make automatic succession possible.

## 4. Alternatives Considered

### Alternative A (Chosen): Declare automatic successor handoff `not possible on this host` and use `state.json` + explicit resume

- **Pros:**
  - Honest to OpenCode `v2.3.2`'s actual session architecture; avoids broken background sessions or parent back-wake loops.
  - Zero new runtime dependencies, zero sidecars, and zero risk of orphaning the user's active TUI/CLI session.
  - Existing `snapshots.json.rootSessionIds` (`tools.ts:1428-1442, 1622-1631`) already aggregates cost across multiple root OpenCode sessions when a run is resumed explicitly.
- **Cons:**
  - Starting a fresh top-level session requires the user to call `teamwork_resume`/`teamwork_next` in that new session (the `/teamwork` template does not yet select this path; see Known gaps) rather than rotating invisibly mid-turn.

### Alternative B (Rejected): Spawn a child successor via `ctx.session.create({ parentID: currentSessionID })`

- **Why rejected:** Because `parentID` binds the new session as a child of the retiring session (`@123,383,940`), every completed round in the child emits a `<subagent>` report into the retiring parent's inbox and wakes the retiring parent session, causing duplicate orchestration turns and compounding token spend.

### Alternative C (Rejected): Spawn an unlinked top-level session via `ctx.session.create({})` and call `ctx.session.prompt`

- **Why rejected:** Runs headless in the background with no way to attach the user's active TUI/CLI viewport to the new `sessionID`, breaking interactive status visibility, permission prompts, and user cancellation.

### Alternative D (Rejected): Call `ctx.session.compact({ sessionID })` at a threshold and label it "successor handoff"

- **Why rejected:** Explicitly forbidden by the [issue #4 contract](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/4) (triage note: [#1 comment](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/1#issuecomment-7074469705)): *"Do not fake a successor by clearing context in place"*. In-place compaction is already handled natively by OpenCode V2 and assisted by `session.hook("context")`.

## 5. Consequences

### Positive
- Prevents silent background session leaks, parent back-wake loops, and TUI detachment on OpenCode V2.
- Preserves the existing `teamwork_resume` + `state.json` + `snapshots.json.rootSessionIds` manual-resume tooling (see Known gaps for the command-template follow-up).

### Negative / Trade-offs
- Unattended multi-hour runs within a single OpenCode session rely on OpenCode's native context compaction plus `session.hook("context")` (`describeRun`) rather than automatic fresh-session rotation.

### Known gaps / follow-ups

These are real limitations of the manual-resume path. None of them change the decision: they concern recovery ergonomics and correctness *within* a session, not session replacement.

- **The `/teamwork` command template does not select the resume path.** As noted in §3 item 2, the template calls `teamwork_plan` unconditionally (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/index.ts:42-43`), so `/teamwork <session-id>` starts a new run. Follow-up: add the explicit resume branch described in §3 item 2 (or a separate `/teamwork-resume <session-id>` command).
- **Interrupted tasks are not re-queued.** `teamwork_next` classifies `worker_active` / `verifier_active` tasks as `inProgress` and never returns them as `readyForWorker` or `readyForVerifier` (`tools.ts:1878-1884`). After an interrupted worker or verifier, the task must be reset explicitly (for example with `teamwork_task_update` back to `pending` or `verified_fail`) before it can be dispatched again.
- **Concurrent resumes can dispatch duplicate workers.** `teamwork_next` reads `state.json` and returns ready tasks without a claim or lease (`tools.ts:1795-1900`), so two concurrent resumes can both observe the same task as dispatchable and both spawn a worker for it.
- **`describeRun(root)` selects the newest run, not the caller's session.** Runs resolved without an explicit `sessionId` take the first entry from `listRuns(root)` (`resolveRun`, `tools.ts:1005`). When multiple runs exist, callers must pass `sessionId` explicitly; the injected context summary may otherwise describe a different run.
- **Interrupted cost updates can double-count.** The cost tool writes `costs.json` and then `snapshots.json` under one lock but not one transaction (`tools.ts:1686-1687`, `1704-1705`). A crash or interrupt between the two writes leaves `snapshots.json` with stale `lastCost` values, so the next invocation re-adds the same session delta.

## 6. Exact Missing Host Capabilities (To Revisit Issue #4)

Issue [#4](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/issues/4) remains blocked on the host until OpenCode V2 exposes **either**:

1. **Active-session replacement / foreground handoff API (`ctx.session.replace` or `ctx.session.handoff`):**
   A host primitive `ctx.session.handoff({ fromSessionID, agent, model, prompt, metadata })` that:
   - Atomically terminates or archives `fromSessionID` so it cannot be woken by future `<subagent>` inbox reports;
   - Creates a fresh session `toSessionID` with clean message history;
   - Rebinds the user's attached TUI/CLI client stream from `fromSessionID` to `toSessionID`; and
   - Reparents or links `fromSessionID` in `session_v2` so session-tree cost queries (`teamwork_cost`) and child subagents recognize `toSessionID`.
2. **Or non-waking parent delegation (`wakeParent: false` on `ctx.session.create`):**
   An option on `ctx.session.create({ parentID, wakeParent: false })` (paired with a persistent thin root Sentinel session that never accumulates worker tool output) allowing a child orchestrator session to spawn a sibling under the same root `parentID` and terminate itself without waking the retired sibling.

# ADR 0004: Post-Open fd Containment for Intermediate-Component Symlink Races in Run-Directory Reads

- **Status:** Proposed (design only; the mitigation is **not** implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Workstream:** Sprint 2, S4a (follow-up to the PR #10 hardening)
- **Classification:** ADR / security design gate
- **Related:** [PR #10](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/opencode-teamwork-v2/pull/10), `docs/ARTIFACTS.md:806-809`, `docs/GUARDRAILS.md:28-43`

## 1. Context

### 1.1 The invariant under attack

Run artifacts live under `<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/` and are treated as untrusted control data (`docs/ARTIFACTS.md:7-38`, `docs/GUARDRAILS.md:6-41`). A reader must not return bytes from a file outside that run directory, even when an attacker can create, rename, or delete entries **inside** the run directory.

The primary read path is:

1. `readBoundedRunFile(run, targetPath, maxBytes)` calls `ensureSafeRunSubpath(run, targetPath)` and then `readBoundedFileNoFollow(check.path, maxBytes)` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:404-408`).
2. `ensureSafeRunSubpath` validates the run directory and every path segment with `lstatSync`, then validates the parent and target with `realpathSync`, and finally returns the resolved target path (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:251-323`).
3. `readBoundedFileNoFollow` opens that returned **path** with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, then uses `fstat` on the returned fd for the authoritative type and size check (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:347-402`, flags at `:352-353`, open at `:363`, `fstat` at `:364`).

There are also two independent CLI readers:

- `lib/export.mjs` has its own `readBounded` (`lib/export.mjs:144-172`) with an `lstatSync` pre-check (`:147`), `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW` open (`:148`), and `fstat` (`:149`). Call sites are `:203`, `:232`, and `:255`.
- `lib/timeline.mjs` has the same implementation (`lib/timeline.mjs:54-82`, pre-check `:57`, open `:58`, `fstat` `:59`). Call sites are `:136` and `:221`.

Those two readers are intentionally not routed through `tournament.ts` (`lib/export.mjs:14-18`, `lib/timeline.mjs:13-16`).

### 1.2 What PR #10 already closed

PR #10 made the **final** path component atomic on POSIX:

- `O_NOFOLLOW` makes the open fail with `ELOOP` if the final component is a symlink.
- `O_NONBLOCK` prevents `open()` from blocking forever on a FIFO.
- `fstat(fd)` is authoritative for the opened inode, so a final component swapped *after* the open cannot change the type or size the reader validates.
- `readSync` retries `EINTR` and fails closed on `EAGAIN` and every other error (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:374-381`).
- The non-POSIX fallback is an `lstat` pre-check and still refuses symlinks and non-regular files, but is explicitly non-atomic (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:354-362`).

The existing FIFO regression test is `scripts/test-engine.mjs:4891-4939`; it runs the reader in a child process with a hard timeout so a blocking regression fails rather than hangs the suite.

### 1.3 What remains

`O_NOFOLLOW` only affects the **final** component. `ensureSafeRunSubpath` performs all of its `lstat`/`realpath` checks *before* `readBoundedFileNoFollow` calls `openSync` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:269-321` versus `:363`). An attacker who can rename an intermediate directory inside the run can therefore make the checked path resolve to a different directory between the check and the open.

The code already documents the gap:

- `plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:342-345`: "`O_NOFOLLOW` protects only the final path component. An intermediate directory swapped for a symlink between the segment checks and the open is still a race; closing it fully needs component-by-component `openat`/`O_PATH` traversal, which is not implemented here."
- `lib/export.mjs:14-18` and `lib/timeline.mjs:13-16` say the same for their readers.
- `docs/ARTIFACTS.md:806-809` records the same limitation in the public artifact contract.

An adversarial review in Sprint 2 demonstrated the bypass: swap an intermediate directory (for example `run/verify/`) for a symlink to an outside directory after the segment checks and before the open, and the reader returns the outside regular file's contents. This ADR responds to that finding. **No fix is claimed here.**

### 1.4 Reproducible shape of the bypass

```text
run/
  verify/            <- real directory during ensureSafeRunSubpath
    report.json      <- inside file, passes every check

attacker: rename(run/verify, run/verify.real)
          symlink(outside_dir, run/verify)      <- now points outside

readBoundedRunFile(run, run/verify/report.json)
  ensureSafeRunSubpath: already passed (saw run/verify as a directory)
  openSync(run/verify/report.json, O_NOFOLLOW)
    -> resolves through the symlinked run/verify
    -> opens outside_dir/report.json
  fstat: regular file, within byte cap
  -> status "ok" with outside contents
```

The final component (`report.json`) is not a symlink, so `O_NOFOLLOW` does not help. The final `fstat` sees a perfectly ordinary regular file; it has no way to know which directory the path resolved through.

The same class applies to the run directory itself: `ensureSafeRunSubpath` calls `lstatSync(run)` and `realpathSync(run)` at `plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:254-258`, and the open happens later by path at `:363`.

### 1.5 Scope of this ADR

In scope: the **read** path used by `readBoundedRunFile`/`readBoundedFileNoFollow`, plus the same pre-check-then-open pattern in `lib/export.mjs` and `lib/timeline.mjs`.

Out of scope but noted:

- The **write** path has the same structural risk. `writeSafeRunFile` validates the target and temp path with `ensureSafeRunSubpath` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:428-436`, `:445`), then `writeFileSync` and `renameSync` operate by path (`:448`, `:453`). A raced intermediate directory can redirect the create/rename outside the run. The read mitigation in this ADR does not fix it.
- `tools.ts` calls `readBoundedFileNoFollow` directly from `readRunText` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts:988-990`), without `ensureSafeRunSubpath`; call sites include `join(run, "ORIGINAL_REQUEST.md")` (`:840`), `join(run, "pitfalls.md")` (`:995`), and `join(run, "prompt_draft.md")` (`:5308`). A bare file path cannot be containment-checked because the low-level reader does not know the run root. The post-open check proposed here therefore belongs in a root-aware primitive (`readWithinBounded(runReal, file, maxBytes)`), and `readRunText` / its call sites must pass the run root so these direct reads get the same check.
- A hardlink inside the run to an outside file is not a path-traversal escape: the inode is reachable from inside the run, and creating the link requires the target to be owned by the process user (or `protected_hardlinks` to be disabled) plus write access to the run directory. It is a separate threat and is not addressed here.

## 2. Threat Model and Impact

### 2.1 Attacker capabilities assumed

- Can create, rename, and delete entries **inside** `<workspace>/.opencode/teamwork/<session-id>/`, including subdirectories.
- Can win a race against a coordinator/verifier/CLI read, or can plant a static intermediate symlink.
- **Cannot** write or rename entries outside the run directory (no write permission on the target directory, no ownership of the target).
- Does not need to be a different OS user. A compromised or prompt-injected agent, a malicious artifact writer, or untrusted run content is enough. The process may hold read permissions the attacker does not directly have (for example, a secret elsewhere in the workspace or in the user's home directory).

### 2.2 Impact

**Containment bypass / information disclosure.** Outside file contents can be pulled into:

- run context injected by `describeRun` / `session.hook("context")` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tools.ts:988-990` and its callers),
- `timeline` and `export` output, and
- reports or logs derived from those reads.

That can leak secrets into prompts, transcripts, or exported artifacts even though the attacker could not read the file directly.

**Not privilege escalation.** Reaching a false `PASS` still requires writing run-dir artifacts (a manifest, a report, a verdict), which run-dir write access already permits. Verdicts are recomputed from evidence, not from injected context (`docs/ARTIFACTS.md:809-813`). The security boundary that is crossed is *containment*: the reader's promise that it only reads inside the run.

### 2.3 Non-goals

- Authenticating run content. A writer inside the run can still forge a manifest or a report; that is accepted by the threat model and is documented at `docs/ARTIFACTS.md:809-813`.
- Defending against an attacker who can write outside the run, control the kernel, mount a malicious `/proc`, or replace the Node binary.
- Preventing the `open()` syscall itself. The proposed control is detective: it refuses to **read or return** bytes after checking the opened fd. It cannot guarantee that the open never touched an outside path, and it cannot undo side effects of opening a special file (the existing `fstat` regular-file check runs before any read).
- Fixing write-path containment.

## 3. Options

### 3.1 Option (a): component-by-component `openat` / `O_PATH` traversal

Walk from a directory fd for the run root, opening each segment relative to the previous directory fd with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY`, then open the final component relative to the last directory fd with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`.

**Pros**

- Preventive and exact: no path re-resolution between validation and open.
- Refuses intermediate symlinks at the syscall boundary, not by a separate check.
- Works for reads and writes if the write path is rewritten the same way.

**Cons**

- Node core has no `openat`/`openat2` API. `fs.open` takes a path, and `fs.constants.O_PATH` is not even defined on the Node v26.13.1 / Linux 7.4 host used for this review (runtime probe).
- A pure-JS Linux workaround exists: after opening a directory fd, `openSync("/proc/self/fd/<dirfd>/<segment>", O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY)` resolves relative to the pinned directory inode. This was verified on the review host. It is still Linux-only, adds one fd per path segment, and is a procfs trick rather than a stable Node API.
- On macOS, `/dev/fd/<fd>` is not guaranteed to support path traversal beneath the fd, and Node exposes no `fcntl(F_GETPATH)` binding. A native addon would be required for a real component-wise traversal.

**Verdict:** the correct long-term primitive, but too large and too platform-specific for this sprint. The Linux procfs variant is a reasonable follow-up once the smaller control is in place.

### 3.2 Option (b): Linux `openat2` with `RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS`

Kernel 5.6+ supports `openat2(2)` with `RESOLVE_BENEATH` (refuse any resolution that escapes the starting directory) and `RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS` (refuse every symlink component). This is the strongest Linux-only guarantee.

**Pros**

- One syscall closes the entire class, including intermediate components.
- `RESOLVE_BENEATH` expresses the containment invariant directly.

**Cons**

- Node core exposes no `openat2` binding. Using it requires a native addon, a helper binary, or an unstable internal binding. All of those violate the package's zero-runtime-dependency constraint and complicate installation on Node >=18 and on non-Linux platforms.
- Kernel/version gating and an `ENOSYS`/`EINVAL` fallback are required.
- `RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS` forbids all symlinks, including a symlinked workspace root; the run root must be resolved first and passed as the `dirfd`, which means the same directory-fd plumbing as option (a).

**Verdict:** an optional fast path only if a zero-dependency binding becomes available. It is not part of the proposed implementation.

### 3.3 Option (c): post-open fd identity / containment check

Keep the existing pre-checks, `O_NOFOLLOW`, `O_NONBLOCK`, and `fstat`. After the open and the regular-file check, resolve the fd's current path and assert it is still under the run's real path:

```text
fd = openSync(path, O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK)
fst = fstatSync(fd)                     // regular file?
if /proc/self/fd exists:
  try fdPath = realpathSync("/proc/self/fd/" + fd)
  catch -> refuse                       // e.g. deleted file: ENOENT
  if fdPath ends with " (deleted)" -> refuse
  rel = relative(runReal, fdPath)
  if !rel || rel.startsWith("..") || isAbsolute(rel) -> refuse
read(fd)
```

**Pros**

- Pure JS, zero dependencies, no native addon, no new package entry point.
- Works on Linux where `/proc/self/fd` is mounted (verified on the review host: `realpathSync("/proc/self/fd/<fd>")` returns the opened file's path).
- Catches the raced intermediate symlink **before any bytes are read**, because the check is placed between `fstat` and the first `readSync`.
- Can cover direct callers such as `readRunText` once they pass the run root to the root-aware primitive; it does not require the full `ensureSafeRunSubpath` policy on every call.
- Small enough to share with the CLI readers (see `docs/spikes/shared-safe-fs.md`).

**Cons**

- Detective, not preventive: the outside file is opened, then refused. For a regular file that is harmless; for a special file, `fstat` refuses before any read, but the open itself still occurred.
- Linux-only in practice. macOS has no pure-JS fd-to-path primitive in Node core (`fcntl(F_GETPATH)` is not bound, and `/dev/fd` path resolution is not guaranteed); Windows has neither. Those platforms keep the current behavior and the residual risk.
- The fd path can change between the check and the read if the attacker can rename the file **outside** the run, which the threat model excludes. Renames **inside** the run are harmless: the bytes are still inside.
- It does not prove the inode was the *intended* child. A run-dir writer can redirect the path to a different file **inside** the run; that is already permitted by run-dir write access and is not a containment breach.
- Requires a documented fail-closed policy when `/proc/self/fd` exists but resolution fails (for example, a deleted file or a restricted `/proc`).

**Verdict:** the smallest portable improvement that actually closes the demonstrated read bypass on Linux. Recommended.

### 3.4 Option (d): accept and document the residual risk

Keep the current code and the known-limitation comments (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:342-345`, `lib/export.mjs:14-18`, `lib/timeline.mjs:13-16`, `docs/ARTIFACTS.md:806-809`).

**Pros:** zero change, zero new platform assumptions.

**Cons:** a demonstrated containment bypass remains in a security-hardening sprint. The mitigation in option (c) is small enough that "accept" is hard to justify on Linux.

**Verdict:** rejected as the primary decision. Keep the documentation current for platforms where (c) is unavailable.

### 3.5 Comparison

| | Preventive | Portable | Zero deps | Node-only | Covers writes | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `openat`/`O_PATH` | yes | no (Linux procfs / native on macOS) | yes on Linux procfs; no on macOS | yes on Linux; native elsewhere | yes if reused | high |
| (b) `openat2` | yes | Linux only | no (native) | no | yes if reused | high |
| (c) post-open fd check | no (detective) | Linux only in practice | yes | yes | no | low |
| (d) accept | no | yes | yes | yes | no | none |

## 4. Decision

**Adopt option (c) for the read path, as a defense-in-depth control, with an optional future option (b) fast path.**

Specifically:

1. **Keep every existing check.** `ensureSafeRunSubpath` remains; `O_NOFOLLOW`, `O_NONBLOCK`, `fstat`, the byte cap, and the `EINTR`/fail-closed handling remain. The post-open check is additive.
2. **Place the check in the root-aware read primitive**, not in the pre-check itself. `readBoundedRunFile` keeps `ensureSafeRunSubpath`, which must also return `runReal`; it then calls `readWithinBounded(runReal, path, maxBytes)`. The bare `readBoundedFileNoFollow(file, maxBytes)` cannot enforce containment because it has no root, so `tools.ts` `readRunText` and its call sites must pass the run root (or the run directory) and use the root-aware primitive for direct reads.
3. **Check before the first read.** Order: `open` -> `fstat` -> regular-file check -> size check -> fd containment -> read. No bytes are read from a refused fd.
4. **Fail closed on ambiguity.** If `/proc/self/fd` exists and the fd path cannot be resolved, or resolves to a path ending in `" (deleted)"`, return `status: "error"` with a `refused:` message. If `/proc/self/fd` does not exist (macOS, Windows, hardened containers), keep the current behavior and the documented residual risk; do not turn every read into an error.
5. **Record the platform boundary.** The guarantee is "on Linux with a mounted `/proc/self/fd`, an outside regular file is never returned." It is not a portable guarantee. Update `docs/ARTIFACTS.md:806-809`, the reader comments, and the guardrails table to say exactly that.
6. **Keep the optional `openat2` fast path out of scope.** If a zero-dependency binding appears, it can be added behind a capability probe; it must not become a required native dependency.
7. **Proposed, not implemented.** This ADR does not claim the code has changed. The acceptance tests in §5 define what "done" means.

What remains unprovable without `openat`-style traversal:

- That the path resolved to the intended directory at the instant of the open. The check proves only that the opened fd's path is inside the run when checked.
- That the open itself had no side effects. `fstat` prevents reading a non-regular file, but it cannot undo an open of a device or FIFO (the latter is non-blocking).
- On macOS and Windows, anything stronger than the current pre-checks.

### 5.4 Race harness (intermediate directory swap)

This is the test that distinguishes the pre-fix and post-fix code.

Parent process (reader):

```js
const run = join(root, "run")
const sub = join(run, "sub")           // real dir with secret.json
const outside = join(root, "outside")  // outside dir with secret.json = SENTINEL

const swapper = spawn(process.execPath, ["-e", swapperCode], {
  env: { ...process.env, SUB: sub, OUTSIDE: outside },

for (let i = 0; i < 2000; i++) {

swapper.kill()
assert(okInside > 0, "harness never read the legitimate inside file")
```

Swapper child (hold each state briefly so both the legitimate read and the race window are exercised):

```js
const sleep = (ms) => Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms)
for (;;) {
  renameSync(SUB, SUB + ".real")
  symlinkSync(OUTSIDE, SUB)
  sleep(0.5)
  renameSync(SUB, SUB + ".link")
  renameSync(SUB + ".real", SUB)
  sleep(0.5)
  unlinkSync(SUB + ".link")
}
```

Assertions:

- Zero results contain `SENTINEL`.
- At least one read succeeds against the legitimate inside file, so the loop is actually exercising the path (not just `ENOENT`).
- The whole test completes under 15 seconds and does not hang or crash.
- Add a **negative control** in the test file: a local `vulnerableRead` that performs the old `lstat`-then-`open` sequence with a deliberate busy-wait between the check and the open. Run the same swapper against it and assert it observes at least one `SENTINEL` read. This proves the harness can detect the bug class; it is not run against production code.
- The zero-leak assertion is a regression guard, not a proof. The negative control is what makes a pass meaningful.

### 5.5 fd containment primitive (deterministic)

If the fix exports a small `fdWithin(runReal, fd)` helper for testing, assert:

3. Open `run/a.txt`, rename it to `outside/a.txt`, then check -> `false` (path is now outside).

5. Open `run/a.txt`, rename the run directory, then check against the old `runReal` -> `false` (fail closed; a false negative is acceptable).

## 6. Consequences

### Positive

- Would close the demonstrated intermediate-directory read bypass on Linux for regular files, before any bytes are returned.
- Covers direct `readBoundedFileNoFollow` callers that skip `ensureSafeRunSubpath`.
- Small, dependency-free, and compatible with Node >=18.
- Composable with the shared safe-fs module proposed in `docs/spikes/shared-safe-fs.md`.

### Negative

- One extra `realpathSync` per read on Linux; negligible against JSON parsing and file I/O.
- A new platform distinction in the security contract: Linux stronger, macOS/Windows unchanged.
- `/proc/self/fd` may be absent or restricted in hardened containers; the fallback must be documented and must not silently claim the stronger guarantee.
- False negatives if the run directory is renamed after `runReal` is computed; the read is refused, which is safe but may surprise callers.

### Residual risks

- The `open()` itself still occurs on the outside path before the check. For regular files this is harmless; the `fstat` regular-file check prevents reading devices/FIFOs.
- macOS and Windows retain the intermediate-component race.
- Write paths retain the same race; `writeSafeRunFile` is not fixed by this ADR.
- A run-dir writer can still forge content inside the run and influence what agents read. That is accepted and documented; verdicts are recomputed from evidence.
- Hardlinks inside the run to outside files are outside this threat model.

### Follow-ups

1. Implement the shared safe-fs module (`docs/spikes/shared-safe-fs.md`) so all three readers get the same check.
2. Evaluate Linux `/proc/self/fd/<dirfd>/<segment>` traversal for a preventive read path, and a native/optional `openat2` path if a zero-dependency binding becomes available.
3. Apply the same analysis to `writeSafeRunFile` (`plugins/opencode-teamwork/tournament.ts:428-457`) and the `tools.ts` writers.
4. Add `O_NONBLOCK` to the `lib/*.mjs` readers, or route them through the shared module, to remove the FIFO-blocking difference.

## 7. Alternatives Rejected

- **(a) component-wise `openat`/`O_PATH` now:** correct, but Node core has no directory-relative open; the Linux procfs workaround is a larger change and does not help macOS. Defer.
- **(b) `openat2` now:** strongest on Linux, but requires a native addon or helper and breaks the zero-dependency/Node-only constraint. Keep as an optional future fast path.
- **(d) accept and document only:** leaves a demonstrated containment bypass that option (c) closes cheaply on the primary platform. Keep the documentation for platforms where (c) is unavailable, not as the decision.

## 8. The Exact Missing Primitive

A directory-fd-relative open in Node core:

```text
openat(dirfd, path, flags)                      // POSIX
openat2(dirfd, path, how)                       // Linux 5.6+, RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS
fcntl(fd, F_GETPATH, buf)                       // macOS fd-to-path
```

Node's `fs` exposes only path-based `open`, and `fs.constants.O_PATH` is not defined on the review host (Node v26.13.1 / Linux 7.4). Without one of those primitives, there is no portable way to prove that the path validated is the path opened. On Linux, `/proc/self/fd/<dirfd>/<segment>` is a usable workaround but is not a cross-platform API and is not used by the proposed patch. On macOS, there is no pure-JS fd-to-path primitive, so option (c) cannot be enforced there without a native binding.
